## `202626081052`: OCR where it pays (10 done, 7 open, PARKED)

This order decides where Leasha should spend time on OCR. It came out of an earlier index run that logged dozens of "nothing to index without OCR" lines for scanned PDFs.

**The decision it records:** OCR scanned PDFs, but don't OCR pictures embedded in Office documents. The reasoning is value density. A scanned standard is 200 pages of text no search can reach. An embedded PowerPoint picture is usually a logo or icon. The order's own estimates (on a borrowed 3.6s/page measurement) are about 4 hours for the scanned PDFs at a 20-page budget, against about 150 hours for embedded Office pictures.

**Done:** the two-pass design (text first, then OCR), `--only-ocr` re-reading the skip ledger instead of re-walking by extension, OCR text labelled `read_by=ocr`, capped reads saying how much they read, and a count of picture-heavy decks in the report.

**Open (7), and they are left open deliberately:**
- **§3, four measurement steps.** Time the S88-S95 scanned-standards folder with the page budget on. Search for text on page 3 and page 30 to see whether 20 pages makes a manual findable or only its cover. Count how many PDFs have no text layer. Record all three. These need your corpus and your machine.
- **§5, a decision and a conditional build.** Decide about Office pictures once the §3 numbers exist. If it's ever built, it needs a ~50KB size floor so bullet graphics are never rendered.

- **Detection:** `app/extract/face_detect.py` uses the `buffalo_l` model pack, and `available()` returns True in your venv.
- **Grouping:** `app/index/face_clustering.py` sorts faces into unnamed "Person 1" piles.
- **Naming:** the store can create, rename, combine and split piles and remove a face from one. It can also forget a person and assign a face to a named pile (`create_pile`, `rename_pile`, `combine_piles`, `split_pile`, `forget_person`, `assign_face`). New faces that closely match a named pile are assigned automatically.
- **Search:** `/who Daddy` filters on named people, so "daddy and me on the beach" can work once names exist.
- **The screen for naming:** `PhotoTaggerPage` in `app/ui/widgets/photo_tagger_page.py`. It has the pile grid, click to name, combine, split, forget and yes/no suggestion chips, and it has its own tests.

<result>The Chat engine is finished and committed on `w/chat-engine` in three commits. All new tests pass, the six `settings_reachable` failures are expected, and the first real-model measurement is below the 85% extractive floor. I did not run the full suite.

## Layout and order mapping
Everything is in `app/chat/`, plus `tests/fixtures/chat_eval.py` and the `tests/unit/test_chat_*.py` files.
- **1a router:** `router.py` (rules first, small model second, answer validated).
- **1b loop:** `engine.py` and `plan.py`, at most 3 rounds, reusing `translate_rules`.
- **1c context economy:** `context.py`.
- **1d aggregates:** `aggregate.py`. The number is `COUNT(*)` inserted into a template; the model never touches it.
- **1e absence protocol:** `absence.py`.
- **2a, 2b, 2c and 4e-1 verification and quotes:** `verify.py`, `text.py`.
- **4a-4c:** `evaluate.py` and `evaluate --chat`.
- **4d roles:** `roles.py`.
- **Sessions:** `sessions.py`.

## Interface as built
The contract is unchanged except for additions.
- `ChatTurn.debug` is a new field with a default.
- `ChatEngine` also has `set_shelf(pinned, excluded)`, `set_model(role, name)`, `roles()`, `suggest_modes()` and `installed_models()`.
- `available()` returns `(bool, reason)`.
- `llm` may be one model or a `{router, planner, answerer}` dict.

`TokenEvent` carries whole verified sentences, never raw model tokens. Sentences carry `[n]` markers numbered by first mention, and `receipts[n-1]` is the source.

## Measurements
Machine: Windows 11, 12 CPUs, 32 GB, CPU-only Ollama, busy with other work.

| Model | Questions | Extractive | Citation validity | Aggregate | Absence honesty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| qwen2.5:1.5b | all 80 | 83.9% (26/31) | 100% (31 sentences, none unreceipted) | 100% | 100% |
| mistral (7B) | 10 | 83.3% (5/6) | 100% (6 sentences, none unreceipted) | n/a | 100% |

- **Extractive:** both are just under the 85% ship floor. I recorded the numbers without lowering the floor.
- **qwen2.5:1.5b latency:** first narration under 0.02s; first answer text p50 2.3s, p95 8.1s.
- **mistral subset (10 questions):** first answer text p50 63s, p95 80s, on a machine that was busy.
- **Other qwen2.5:1.5b results:** router, find, refusal and trap questions were all 100%; synthesis was 20% (no floor at v1).
- **FakeLLM:** 80 questions, extractive 96.8%, aggregate 100%, absence 100%. These numbers describe the engine, not a language model.
- **Fixture:** 80 QA pairs across all six router classes (planted absences, trap questions, follow-ups).

## Floors pinned as tests
The pins are in `test_chat_evaluate.py`:
- Citation validity at least 98%.
- Extractive at least 90%, measured with FakeLLM.
- Aggregate exactness 100%.
- Absence honesty 100%.
- Router at least 97%.
- Find at least 95%.
- Refusal at least 60%.
- Traps at least 50%.
- Synthesis at least 60%.

Setting `LEASHA_CHAT_REAL_MODEL=<ollama model>` enables an opt-in real-model test.

All on surface `settings.models`, using `setObjectName(KEY)` and a saved `{KEY: value}`:
- `CHAT_MODEL`, `CHAT_ROUTER_MODEL`, `CHAT_PLANNER_MODEL` (text, default empty).

- `CHAT_VERIFY_STRICTNESS` (int 30..90, default 70).

Schema version 26 adds the `chat_sessions` table. The store has `save_session(id, title, turns, shelf, model)`, `load_sessions(with_turns=True)` and `delete_session(id)`. Another engineer may also add a v26; the lead should resolve that on merge.

claim:
The single-process full run started at 22:52, and I'm watching it for progress and for a crash.

**The silent-crash cause:** the test suite was running real OCR, embedding and reranking models on your graphics card. On this machine the `auto` device setting picks DirectML, and after about a thousand tests a later DirectML run access-violated and killed pytest without a trace. It ended three full runs. Pinning the OCR and embedding devices to the CPU made the exact crashing set complete with a normal exit.

**The fix:** `tests/conftest.py` now defaults `EMBED_DEVICE` to `cpu` and pins OCR to it. Setting `EMBED_DEVICE=auto` still runs the tests against the card on purpose. It also stops the suite competing with your live app for the GPU. I reverted my subprocess workaround, so the OCR test is original again and passes in-process.

**Fixed:**

- The video and audio words in the `/type` menu.
- The space-report JSON test (the change was intentional).
- The index-bench timing flake.
- The settings scanner skipping the chat reader.
- The stale "memory" filter test.
- The redesign test now allows the Space Report tabs.
- **User-facing bug:** the Chat page took keyboard focus, so arrowing down the rail got stuck at Chat with Reports, Indexing and Settings unreachable. It's fixed with the guard the other pages already use.

One thing to know: the native crash is real on this machine, so it may also be a risk in the running app if it uses DirectML for OCR and embedding at scale. I haven't shown that it is. Your `.env` says `EMBED_DEVICE=cpu`, so the app isn't affected today. I'll list it as an open item.
